requirement:
TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a value on the same line. A `#` inside a quoted
string belongs to the string.
rationale:
The subject, `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments`, has three obligations. TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment, including a trailing comment after a value. A `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string.

The only test is the `test.toml` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. It carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. Its source is:
`# first\n# second\na = '# literal' # real\n"# key" = """# literal"""\n`

The test collects every attachment from the outline items and sorts them by span start. It then asserts the exact list of `(kind, text)` pairs. For this case the expected list is `(Comment, "# first")`, `(Comment, "# second")` and `(Comment, "# real")`.

| Obligation | How the test checks it |
|---|---|
| Only `Comment` attachments | Every expected kind is `Comment`, and the assertion compares the whole list. Any `Annotation` or other kind would fail it. |
| Each `#` comment is one attachment | `# first` and `# second` are adjacent comment lines. The test expects them as two separate attachments, not one merged attachment. |
| Trailing comment after a value | `a = '# literal' # real` must yield `# real` as its own attachment. |
| `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string | There are three string forms: a literal string `'# literal'` as a value, a basic-string key `"# key"`, and a multi-line basic string `"""# literal"""`. The test expects no attachment for any of them. |

Because the assertion is exact equality on the full list, it would reject both spurious attachments from string contents and missing or merged comments. The same test also checks that plain text yields no attachments, but that belongs to a different requirement.

I found no obligation in the text that lacks a test. Cases the text does not name are not required, for example `'''` multi-line literal strings, escaped quotes inside strings, and comments with no following item. There are no acknowledgments, and none are needed.
